papers_read.title_as_printed: Multimodal Convolutional Mixer for Mild Cognitive Impairment Detection (Grigas, Damasevicius and Maskeliunas, Comput Mater Contin 2025;84(1), doi 10.32604/cmc.2025.064354)

Automated classification of Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment, and cognitively normal patients using 3D convolutional neural network and radiomic features from T1-weighted brain MRI: A comparative study on detection accuracy (Zarei et al., Clinical Imaging 2024;115:110301)

what_each_reports.P-359: Multimodal ConvMixer (MCM-768) on fused mid-slice T1w MRI + PiB-PET images concatenated with MMSE, CDR and FAQ scores, education, gender and blood pressure, MCI vs CN: accuracy 96.39% (sensitivity 96.90%, specificity 95.87%) on the MCSA dataset alone (412/412), sagittal plane, random 85/15 split; 94.92% on the pooled ADNI (27/27) + MCSA + OASIS3 (134/134) dataset. Removing the cognitive-test features gives the largest accuracy drop.
what_each_reports.P-66: 3D CNN + radiomic features from bilateral hippocampus and amygdala (FSL-FIRST ROIs) of T1-weighted ADNI MRI, with age and sex, MCI vs CN: fusion accuracy 72.7% (AUC 0.80), radiomics alone 71.6%, CNN alone 69.0%; 200 MCI and 200 CN subjects (948 and 853 images), 5-fold cross-validation with an 80/20 split of images.

quantity_a: Accuracy of MCI vs CN classification in the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging using fused structural MRI + amyloid PiB-PET together with MMSE, CDR and FAQ scores (the tests that enter the clinical diagnosis), on a random internal split.
quantity_b: Accuracy of MCI vs CN classification in ADNI using hippocampal and amygdala ROI images and radiomic features of T1-weighted MRI plus age and sex only.
incompatible_if_same: No. P-359 itself shows that without its non-imaging and attention components performance drops to the same range: its MCM models without multi-head self-attention reach 66-80% on MCSA, and its image-based baselines (ResNet, ViT, DenseNet, MobileNet) reach about 65-75% on MCSA, in line with P-66's 69-72.7%. Neither paper claims an ordering on the other's input set.

gates.task: match in the broad sense (MCI vs CN detection, T1); the registry codes P-66 as T3.
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: the quoted 96.3% is from the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging only; P-66 is ADNI. ADNI contributes only 27/27 subjects to P-359's pooled set. The record's dataset_equal 'Yes' is wrong; no waiver on record.
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal (P-359 random 85/15 split for the quoted figure; P-66 five-fold CV).
gates.modality_family: mismatch: P-359 fuses structural MRI with amyloid PET (PiB) and adds cognitive/functional test scores; P-66 is structural MRI only. The record's 'structural_mri' for both is wrong; no waiver on record.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: same metric type (accuracy) but different cohorts (MCSA vs ADNI) and different predictor sets. P-359 includes MMSE, CDR and FAQ, which are part of how MCI is defined, so its accuracy partly measures agreement with its own diagnostic inputs; P-66 uses no cognitive scores.
performance_validity: The flag's numeric threshold is not reached (0.963 < 0.97), but the figure is near-ceiling from a single random internal split, with diagnostic cognitive scores among the inputs; P-359 reports LODO and 5-fold CV only as plane-averaged figures. P-66 splits by image rather than subject (2403 images of 599 subjects), so subject-level leakage cannot be ruled out; this would inflate, not lower, P-66's figure.
independence: Independent: different authors and, for the compared figure, different cohorts (MCSA vs ADNI).
grounds: The dataset-family gate fails: P-359's 96.3% comes from the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging, and P-66's 72.7% from ADNI.
The modality family and predictor sets differ: fused T1 MRI plus amyloid PiB-PET plus MMSE/CDR/FAQ in P-359, against hippocampal and amygdala T1 ROIs plus age and sex in P-66.
P-359's own ablations show that the cognitive-test features drive its accuracy; its imaging-only baselines perform in P-66's range.
No waiver of either failed gate is recorded.

evidence_quotes.quote: This study integrates multiple data modalities—T1-weighted MRI, Pittsburgh Compound B (PiB) PET scans, cognitive assessments such as Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) and Functional Activities Questionnaire (FAQ), blood pressure parameters, and demographic data—to improve MCI detection.
achieves a classification accuracy of 96.3% on the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging (MCSA) dataset (sagittal plane)
The dataset was divided into training and validation sets with a ratio of 85/15.
Removing cognitive test features (MMSE, CDR, and FAQ) results in the highest drop in accuracy (except for omitting motion correction and PVC in PiB-PET preprocessing)

In the term of MCI vs CN, radiomic-based algorithm alone obtained ACC of 71.6 % and AUC of 77.8, CNN-based algorithm obtained ACC of 69 % and AUC of 75 and their fusion showed ACC of 72.7 % and AUC of 80.
The initial step involved randomly dividing the MRI data for each classification dataset into a sizeable training and validation set (80 % of images) and a testing set (20 % of images).

record_defects: dataset_equal 'Yes': the quoted P-359 figure (96.3%) is from MCSA only, not ADNI.
modality_family 'structural_mri' for both: P-359 fuses T1 MRI with PiB amyloid PET and adds cognitive, clinical and demographic features.

Registry P-359 Best_Metric 'Acc 89.1': 89.1% is the full-dataset sensitivity; full-dataset accuracy is 94.9% and MCSA sagittal accuracy 96.3%. Registry Dataset 'ADNI' misstates the main source (MCSA 412/412; ADNI 27/27).
Registry P-66 Task_Type 'T3' while the record treats it as T1 (the compared result is MCI vs CN detection).
resolution_note is a list of unrelated bridging figures and gives no reason for the false-positive status.
what_would_change_the_verdict: An imaging-only P-359 result on ADNI MCI vs CN that was incompatible with P-66's 69-72.7%; P-359 reports no such figure, and its imaging-only baselines agree with P-66.
